card.architecture: FLUX.2 rectified-flow DiT (~32B, Mistral-Small-3.2-24B encoder), whole-image img2img redraw
card.summary: Reinterpret an entire existing image through FLUX.2-dev using a prompt — the source is used as the init latent and re-sampled at a partial denoise with NO mask, so the composition is kept but the whole frame is redrawn with the family's best prompt understanding, typography and photorealism. The heaviest redraw here (~32B, Q4_K_M): encoder and model load sequentially so each fits 24 GB.
card.pick_when: You want the highest-fidelity whole-image redraw available and can afford FLUX.2-dev's cost.

prompt.guidance: LLM-style prose (Mistral encoder); front-load the key subject. Lower the redraw strength to stay close to the source composition; raise it to let FLUX.2 reinterpret more.
prompt.example: A weathered lighthouse on a storm-lashed cliff at dusk, beam cutting through rain, huge crashing waves, dramatic volumetric light, photorealistic, 35mm
prompt.instructions:
Type the FULL description of the picture you want — this is a whole-frame re-render, not an edit instruction, and FLUX.2-dev follows natural-language prose.
20 steps, euler/simple, distilled guidance 4 (real CFG stays 1).
'Redraw strength' (denoise) controls how far the result drifts from the source: ~0.3-0.5 keeps the source's structure and mostly restyles it, ~0.7+ substantially reinvents it.
The source is normalized to the configured ~1 MP working budget with its aspect ratio preserved, so low-resolution inputs gain a larger VAE grid and oversized inputs are reduced before sampling.
Negative prompts are inactive: the model is guidance-distilled and runs at CFG 1.

ui_help.note: Send an image + a description; the whole frame is redrawn through FLUX.2-dev. 'Redraw strength' controls how far it drifts from the source.
ui_help.good_for: the highest-quality whole-image redraw, keeping composition

edit_use_cases: whole-image img2img: redraw an entire image through FLUX.2-dev from a prompt, keeping composition (highest fidelity)
